q7.answer: Clients no longer copy the key in __init__. At each outbound call they read the key from the current in-memory snapshot (e.g. secrets.get('payments_api_key')) and build the Authorization header. The 5-minute refresh swaps in a new snapshot atomically, so the next call sees the new key. A call already in flight keeps the value it read.

q8.answer: Each pod logs its version ids at startup and on change, and exports per-secret version id and refresh age as metrics. In rollout step 5 the team checks in the metrics service that all 4 pods show the version ids recorded when the new keys were written. They also check the pod list for any pre-migration image, and wait 10 minutes (two refresh intervals). Step 6 then checks the provider's last-used data for the old key, and revocation happens only after both pass.

q9.answer: 1) Set up the store, KMS keys and access policies and test them. 2) Build the code change in a PR (reads from the store, CI guard, api_key lines deleted) and test it in staging with sandbox keys. 3) Create new keys at the providers (old stay valid), test them and write them to the prod store, and make the CI guard required. 4) Merge and roll out; the new image no longer has the keys in config/app.yaml. 5) Confirm all pods are on the new keys, then check the old keys are idle. 6) Revoke the old keys. The removal from the committed file ships with the app switch in the same PR, not as a separate step.

q10.answer: make run reads orders-api/dev/* from the store, which holds sandbox keys, using the engineer's own identity. Engineers have read on dev and no read on prod. APP_ENV defaults to dev and never prod. make run-offline uses a stub backend and fake local provider servers with no store or keys.

q11.answer: It treats it as a failed load. It retries 3 times, 2 seconds apart (4 attempts total). If a secret is still missing, it logs an error without values and exits non-zero. It never turns ready with a partial snapshot, because /healthz returns 503 until all three keys are loaded.
